# Getting Started

sqlpipe copies data from a source database to a target database.

## Install

Open a terminal on Linux or macOS.

Run `curl -sSL https://get.sqlpipe.dev | sh`.

The install script needs network access.

The script downloads sqlpipe and installs it on your PATH.

If the `sqlpipe` command is not found, restart the terminal.

## Configure

Create a file named sqlpipe.yaml in your project directory.

Add the connection details for the source database.

Add the connection details for the target database.

Each database needs a valid connection URL or host settings.

Use the host names and ports from your existing database client.

See the configuration reference for all fields in sqlpipe.yaml.

Before you run sqlpipe, save the file.

## First run

Run `sqlpipe run --config sqlpipe.yaml`.

sqlpipe connects to the source, reads the data, and writes it to the target.

A successful run prints a summary to the terminal.

If the run fails, read the error message in the terminal output.
